key_insight: Intimately bonded, twisted lithium niobate interfaces form nanoscale structural helices whose torsional strain implies chiral dipolar helices, distinct from moiré patterns.
engineering_relevance: Coupling interfacial twist to elastic strain and ferroelectric polarization offers a route to chiral oxide architectures and a distinct form of twistronics.
method: Map interfacial contrast with 4D STEM and differential phase contrast imaging.
Model electron channeling along helical pathways and directly image structural helices using electron ptychography.
Assess chirality through sample-inversion imaging and second-harmonic optical circular dichroism.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports directly imaged structural helices, unchanged DPC images after sample inversion, and unusually large interfacial optical dichroism signals.
watch_item: Dipolar helices are inferred from strain coupling through piezoelectric tensors and flexoelectric coefficients rather than directly imaged in the reported abstract.
